# ERD and database decisions, 21 Oct 2026 (D-27 to D-51)

**Status:** decided by Ibrahim on 21 Oct 2026 (answers to `ERD_DB_APPROVAL_QUESTIONS.md` Q-01 to Q-14, plus the Redis removal; D-46 to D-48 answer N-01, N-02 and N-05 the same evening; D-49 answers N-09 on the Brain side, with the Canonical contract unsigned).
**Precedence:** these rows extend `docs/BLUEPRINT_FINAL.md` §10. Where they conflict with an older decision, they win, and the older row is marked there.
**Applied in:** the generator (`brain_db/tools/schema_gen`, OD-24) and regenerated files, the contracts, `contracts/internal/BRAIN_CONTRACTS.md` and `docs/TEAM_TASKS.md`. The impact list and the verification evidence are in `IMPACT_2026-10-21_ERD_DECISIONS.md`.

| ID | From | Decision | What it changes |
|---|---|---|---|
| D-27 | Redis | **No Redis container at all.** The Brain syncs ERP data only by polling the Canonical API (D-23 to D-25). Event deduplication, stream acknowledgements and dead letters are gone. Failure tracking (`ingest_failure`), checkpoints, idempotency and audit stay. The ERP's own transactional outbox is **not** removed: it is registered in the ERP code (`IOutboxService`) and the ERP blueprint uses it for branch sync, so it has other purposes | Blueprint, compose (task BB-22), D-08 stays superseded |
| D-28 | Q1 (blueprint) | **Retrain every night** in the end-of-day run. No weekly retrain | `training_run.trigger` without `weekly_full` |
| D-29 | Q-01 | `action_proposal.proposed_by IN ('rules','agent')`. Rule proposals may have NULL `session_id` and `requested_by_actor_id`. Agent proposals must have both (CHECK). Every write still needs a human approval | `spec_agent.py` |
| D-30 | Q-02 | **At most one live proposal** (`pending`, `approved`, `executing`) per recommendation, enforced by a partial unique index. Under concurrent creates the loser gets a unique violation and returns the existing proposal. This complements the ERP `Idempotency-Key` (D-09); it does not replace it | `spec_agent.py`, BB-17 |
| D-31 | Q-03 | **Per-product model selection without per-product training.** `model_registry.scope` is `shared` (one artifact fitted across the tenant's products, `product_id` NULL) or `product` (the model a product is served by, with its own backtest WAPE). A product row either points at a shared row via `shared_model_id` (it has no artifact of its own) or has its own artifact (a product-specific LightGBM, allowed only when it beats the shared one on the same time-based backtest) or is artifact-less (seasonal-naive). Selection uses the same rolling-origin backtest and WAPE for every candidate. Separate per-SKU training is not required | `spec_intel.py`, BB-10 |
| D-32 | Q-04 | MVP forecasting families are **seasonal-naive and LightGBM only**. `holt_winters` removed from the seed and from the allowed families | `gen_core.py`, `spec_intel.py`, `contracts_jsonb.py` |
| D-33 | Q-05 | `artifact_format IN ('lightgbm_txt','json')`. Models are produced by our own training job, saved locally in the configured artifact storage, SHA-256 verified on load, written only by brain-worker, with versioned metadata. Pickle and joblib are never loaded. Nothing is downloaded from outside | `spec_intel.py`, BB-10 |
| D-34 | Q-11 | **Multi-tenancy is a core requirement from the start** (supersedes D-16; amends OD-23). Tenant = ERP organization (`organization_id`), taken from the verified auth context, never from a request field. Every tenant-owned row, query, update, delete, job, cache entry, model artifact, forecast, recommendation and agent action is tenant scoped. `tenant_id` columns have **no default**. Shared artifacts are shared only across products of the same tenant. Automated cross-tenant isolation tests are mandatory. PostgreSQL RLS is a **separate** decision (pending, question N-02) | `spec_lib.py` (no default), contracts, BB-24 |
| D-35 | Q-06 | `feature_daily.y_units = GREATEST(net_units, 0)`. `sales_fact` keeps the original `units_sold`, `units_returned`, `net_units` (negative allowed). Days where returns exceed sales are flagged, not silently trusted (how: question N-03). Only complete, validated days are trained on. Net units are recorded sales, not unconstrained customer demand: returns may belong to sales of other days, and stock-outs hide demand (OD-10) | BB-09, BB-10, docs |
| D-36 | Q-07 | **No revenue** in the MVP. No money columns in `sales_fact` without an explicit contract change | none (already true) |
| D-37 | Q-08 | Scopes: `brain:read` (Brain reads), `brain:admin` (job status only; it grants no job execution and no ERP action), `agent:approve` (approve or reject). Scopes are issued by the ERP Identity module from the user's ERP permissions; the Brain has no identity system of its own. Exact scope per endpoint is in `brain.openapi.yaml` | OpenAPI, BB-15, EXT-S1 (Ahmed Salah) |
| D-38 | Q-09 | Manual runs only through `brain-worker run <job>` (e.g. `end_of_day`). No UI button and no job-request API. The scheduler is the normal path. Re-runs must be safe and recorded | BB-16 |
| D-39 | Q-10 | Ingestion, features, recommendations and Brain read APIs (and `brain_db`) are owned by **Ibrahim** (confirms D-02). Not reassigned to Abdelrahman without Ibrahim's agreement | `spec_ingest.py`, `spec_agent.py`, `tpl/01.md`, `tpl/04.md`, TEAM_TASKS |
| D-40 | Q-12 | Intraday anomaly = spikes only. Drops only for closed, complete days. Missing or open days are never zero | BB-12 |
| D-41 | Q-13 | Development, integration tests and the demo use a **synthetic pharmacy dataset** matching the Canonical contracts. Every evaluation result on it is labelled "synthetic data" and is not evidence of real-world accuracy | BB-04, BB-03, BB-20 |
| D-42 | Q-14 | Ibrahim fixes `guard_proposal_transition` himself, guided step by step (task BB-05G, `Answers/02_guided_fix_guard_proposal_transition.md`). Success is claimed only when the tests pass on PostgreSQL 16 | BB-05G |
| D-43 | BB-05G review | **A failed proposal needs a fresh human approval.** `failed → approved` requires a new `action_approval` round (agent:approve, hash-bound, same tenant, immutable, audited as `proposal.approved` with `status_from=failed`); the old approval never re-opens it, and every attempt must use the latest round while the proposal is `executing`. The worker's same-key retries while `executing` (`BRAIN_CONTRACTS.md` §9, up to 3) stay; they resend the same Idempotency-Key and body, which reconciles the original write | `spec_agent.py`, `BRAIN_CONTRACTS.md` §6, §9, `brain_ports.py`, `brain.openapi.yaml` |
| D-44 | BB-05G review | **Approval validity.** Every approval (first or re-approval) authorises execution while `now() <= decided_at + 24 h`; `decided_at` is the database server time of that human decision (a client value is ignored). A re-approval's window starts at its own decision, not at the first approval or the proposal's `expires_at`. The database checks it on `-> approved`, `approved -> executing` and every execution attempt (first send and worker retry); the attempt row is inserted immediately before the ERP write. Hash, tenant, `agent:approve`, audit and idempotency rules are unchanged | `spec_agent.py`, `BRAIN_CONTRACTS.md` §9, `brain.openapi.yaml` |
| D-45 | BB-05G review | **Separate `brain_worker` database role.** brain-worker uses its own login (`BRAIN_WORKER_DB_URL`) granted `brain_worker`: least-privilege table grants, no `INSERT` on `action_approval`, column-level `UPDATE` on `action_proposal`, and the lifecycle trigger lets it only expire proposals and complete executions. No runtime role is superuser, owner or member of another. The database still cannot prove a human acted: brain-api records a decision only after verifying the JWT actor, `agent:approve`, tenant and payload hash; decisions with a `system:` actor are refused | `gen_core.py`, `spec_*.py`, `BRAIN_CONTRACTS.md` §8, §10, `brain.env.example` |
| D-46 | N-01 | **Tenant registry and per-tenant Canonical credentials.** `ingest.tenant_registry` is the stable list of tenants (ERP organizations) the Brain serves. brain-worker runs jobs only for `active` tenants, and brain-api refuses a token whose tenant is not active (403 `TENANT_NOT_ACTIVE`). Each tenant has its **own** Canonical API credential. The database stores only a reference (`credential_ref`) and the SHA-256 of the validated value; the secret lives in the secret store (`CANONICAL_CREDENTIALS_DIR`, Docker secrets) and never in a database column, git or logs. Provisioning goes through a separate `brain-provision` command on its own `brain_provisioner` login. A tenant is created `provisioning` and the database refuses to activate it until its credential was validated (a Canonical read with it returned that tenant id) and an active `rule_config` exists for every rule set. Migrations insert no tenant. Every job uses the credential of the tenant being processed, and a credential whose hash does not match the registry is refused for that tenant only | `spec_tenancy.py`, `gen_core.py` (migration 0007), `BRAIN_CONTRACTS.md` §7.4, §7.5, §7.9, §10, `brain_ports.py` §4.0, `brain.env.example`, `brain.openapi.yaml`, BB-06, BB-15, BB-16, BB-25 (new), EXT-S1 |
| D-47 | N-02 | **PostgreSQL row-level security as an additional wall**, alongside mandatory application-level tenant scoping (D-34 rules stay). Every tenant table has `ENABLE` + `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` and `pol_tenant_isolation` (`tenant_id = public.brain_current_tenant()` for reads and writes). The tenant comes from verified authentication context only (JWT for brain-api, the registry row for brain-worker) and is set per transaction with `set_config('app.tenant_id', …, true)`, never per session, so pooled connections never carry it. A pool checkout hook discards a connection that still carries a tenant. No context means no rows and no writes. No runtime role or login is `SUPERUSER`, `BYPASSRLS` or a table owner, and the services check this at startup. Views use `security_invoker`. Single exception: brain_worker may list registry rows to discover tenants. **Isolation is claimed only for what the checks show:** `tenancy_rls_checks.py` covers the database side for both runtime roles; the application side is BB-24 | `gen_core.py` (migration 0007), `role_security_checks.py`, `tenancy_rls_checks.py` (new), `BRAIN_CONTRACTS.md` §7.12, BB-05, BB-24, `brain_db/docs/03` §2.3 |
| D-48 | N-05 | **Organization-level grain for the MVP:** sales and forecasting per `(tenant_id, product_id, business_date)` for the whole organization. Branch-level forecasting is deferred (no schema change; adding `location_id` later is a breaking migration). The Brain never sums branch or location stock and never uses a location-scoped `InventoryItem` in risk or recommendations without a defined and tested aggregation rule: such a product is not assessable (`INVENTORY_UNAVAILABLE`). The contracts state the supported grain. **ERP behaviour not assumed:** branch-summed sales totals, the organization-wide day close and the draft-PO branch are open questions for Yasin (N-10, EXT-Y1). How organization stock is represented is decided by D-49; a null `location_id` never means organization stock (corrected 21 Oct, night) | `spec_ingest.py` (docs), `BRAIN_CONTRACTS.md` §7.13, C-13, `brain_ports.py` `InventorySnapshot`, `brain.openapi.yaml`, BB-06, BB-13, EXT-Y1 |
| D-49 | N-09 | **Organization inventory as its own record (Option B), with Option D as the fallback.** (1) `canonical.OrganizationInventory` is a separate schema with no `location_id`: ERP-computed `on_hand`, `reserved`, `available` over the locations it marks `included`, every location of the organization listed with `location_status` and `stock_status` (`included`, `excluded_inactive`, `unavailable`) and `stock_as_of`, plus `locations_included` and `complete`. The schema text says exactly what the total means; in-transit stock is excluded. (2) `canonical.InventoryItem` is per location only: `location_id` is required and non-null, `inventory_scope = "location"`; a null is rejected, never interpreted. (3) The Brain does not trust `complete=true` alone: it checks tenant, arithmetic, count, the location set against `canonical.LocationList` (`GET /locations`), completeness and per-location freshness (BRAIN_CONTRACTS §7.13, V0–V8); any failure makes the product not assessable (`INVENTORY_UNAVAILABLE`). The Brain never sums branch stock and never caches organization stock. (4) **Option D:** `rule_config` `platform.inventory_source` defaults to `"none"`, so no inventory-dependent recommendation (`create_purchase_order`) is produced; it is set to `"organization_inventory"` per tenant only after the ERP owners confirm the guarantees. If they cannot, D stays for the MVP. (5) Multi-branch tenants still see recommendations, but creating a proposal returns 409 `CONFLICT`, detail `BRANCH_DECISION_REQUIRED`, while the location register lists more than one active location, until N-10 defines the target branch. (6) The Canonical contract changes are **unsigned** until the ERP owners approve them (EXT-Y1). N-10 and N-11 are not assumed | `schemas/canonical/organization_inventory`, `location_list`, `inventory_item`; fixtures (valid, invalid, `semantic_invalid`); `canonical.openapi.yaml`; `brain.openapi.yaml` description; `brain_ports.py`; `contracts_jsonb.PlatformParams.inventory_source`; BRAIN_CONTRACTS §7.13, C-13, C-15; BB-02, BB-04, BB-06, BB-13, BB-14, BB-17, BB-21, EXT-Y1. No database change |
| D-50 | B2 (readiness audit) | **Migrations run without a superuser.** The five runtime roles are created once per cluster by a role administrator with CREATEROLE (`ddl/bootstrap_roles.sql`), never by a migration run as a non-superuser and never by the migration owner, which has no role attributes. Revisions 0005 and 0007 keep their original role statements for a superuser migrator (behaviour unchanged); any other migrator only verifies that the roles exist and are NOLOGIN NOSUPERUSER NOCREATEDB NOCREATEROLE NOREPLICATION NOBYPASSRLS, which is the guarantee the old `ALTER ROLE` gave. `alembic/env.py` checks the same before the first revision, so a missing bootstrap commits nothing. A database built earlier by a superuser is handed to the migration owner once by a DBA (`ddl/handover_ownership.sql`). Later grant changes (B1, B7) are an additive revision 0008, never an edit of 0005 | `gen_core.py` (`role_block`, `bootstrap_roles_sql`, `handover_ownership_sql`), regenerated 0005, 0007, `brain_db_mvp.sql`, `alembic/env.py`, `brain.env.example`, BB-05, BB-22 |
| D-51 | B1, B7 (readiness audit) | **Least privilege per runtime role, rule-set changes only through provisioning.** (1) `brain_app` (brain-api) reads every `ingest`/`feat`/`intel` table and `rule_config` but writes none of them; it writes only the API's own tables (sessions, messages, agent actions, proposals, decisions, executions, `llm_usage`, `audit_log`), with column-level `UPDATE` of the proposal lifecycle columns instead of table-level `UPDATE`, and has no `DELETE` anywhere. (2) `brain_worker` gets `INSERT, UPDATE` on `feat.calendar_day` (the per-tenant calendar seed and refresh, BB-09); nothing else changes for it. (3) Rule-set versions are added and switched only by `brain_provisioner` (the `brain-provision` command), which gets column-level `UPDATE (is_active)` on `rule_config` and `INSERT` on `audit_log`; RLS keeps it in one tenant per transaction. A caller's-rights trigger refuses any rule-set change without `app.actor_id` and writes `rule_config.version_added` / `.activated` / `.deactivated` audit rows in the same transaction; a deferred constraint trigger refuses a commit that leaves an active tenant without an active version of a set. (4) Additive migration `0008_least_privilege`, generated from `spec_privileges.py`; 0005-0007 are not edited and the downgrade restores the exact 0007 grants. The retention role's read of `tenant_registry` under RLS is out of scope and stays a documented open issue. | `tools/schema_gen/spec_privileges.py` (new), `gen_core.py`, `ddl/0008_least_privilege.sql` + `.down.sql`, `ddl/brain_db_mvp.sql`, `alembic/versions/0008_least_privilege.py`, generated docs 03/04, `verification/role_security_checks.py` (49 checks), `verification/tenancy_rls_checks.py` (10 brain_app checks rewritten on its own tables, plus calendar and rule-set tests; 115 checks). brain-api code that wrote pipeline tables must call the worker or the provisioner instead (none exists yet) |
